B rev 3 — back-to-back poles, set-screw ports, M8 studs + universal bus, 10 hold-down screws

  • Hold-down: 10 counterbored M4 screws.
    • + bar: 4 (−110, −56, 73, 137).
    • − bar: 3 (−110, −55, 46.5).
    • U: 3 (87, 108, 174).
    • The bars are 10 mm longer at the ends to fit the end screws. Screws in the tall port blocks are counterbored down to the stud-field level, clear of the port bores.
  • Fuse-ready link: the link studs moved from 50.0 to 50.8 mm pitch, which is exactly the Bussmann AMG (MEGA-type) bolt-in fuse pitch. The strap or an AMG fuse bolts onto the same M8 studs.
    • The notches are 14.8 mm deep and the U bar has a relief, so the fuse body clears. Clash-checked in Fusion: 0.46 mm clearance under the body, and the terminals touch only their own two bars.
  • Everything else is as in B rev 2: universal bus, one link only, plugs, stow slot, 4 mm solid floor.

B rev 2 — back-to-back poles, set-screw ports, M8 studs + universal bus

  • B brought to the rev 2 standard: lug pockets milled into the aluminium, and 2 counterbored M4 screws per bar into blind inserts in printed bosses.
  • Universal bus U: a separate 6061 bar next to the − bar. It has its own 4 mm wall to − (26 mm metal gap) and the main barrier to + (32 mm). It has 3 × M8 studs (Klauke 4R8 keep-out, up to 4 AWG) exiting rearward.
  • One bolted aluminium strap (6 × 20, ø8.5 holes at 50 mm pitch) ties U to − (through notch N) or to + (through notch P), landing on M8 link studs on bare aluminium. The unused notch takes a printed plug that the cover holds down; the spare plug sits in a park socket. With U floating, the strap goes in an insulated stow slot. There is only one strap, so it can never bridge + to −. The model shows it tied to −.
  • The + bar keeps 2 spares (1 × M8 + the 1/0 port); U adds 3 studs to whichever pole it is tied to.
  • − Longest of the three (325 mm) and the heaviest.

B rev 1 — back-to-back poles, 1/0 set-screw ports + M8 studs

  • Saved exactly as built before the rev 2 changes. The files were restored from the untouched copy, and the Fusion document ST185_busbar_B was put back to this version (v4, promoted to v7; all versions kept).
  • Poles sit back to back: + bar at the front (wires leave forward), − bar at the back (wires leave rearward), with a barrier wall between them.
  • 1/0 cables go into set-screw ports (Weidmüller H50,0/25 ferrule, two M8 cup-point set screws in coil inserts). 4/8 AWG lugs go on M8 studs.
  • Lug pockets are in printed locator plates. Bars are clamped by plate tabs into blind inserts in printed ledges.

A rev 2 — inline poles, two stepped rows, studs only

  • Poles sit end to end: + bar on the left, − bar on the right, with a 4 mm printed wall that runs up to the cover (24 mm metal gap).
  • Each pole has two rows, stepped 6 mm: front-row wires leave forward and rear-row wires leave rearward, so no wires cross.
  • Lug pockets are milled 3 mm deep into the aluminium. Each lug sits flat on bare aluminium, and the metal walls stop it turning.
  • Hold-down: 2 counterbored ISO 7380 M4×10 screws per bar into blind brass inserts in printed bosses under the bar.
  • + Standard lugs everywhere, matching the harness drawings. Nothing to re-torque. Shortest of the three.
  • − Wires leave on both sides, so it needs about 45 mm of free space in front and behind.

Fuse or fusible link in place of the strap?

  • Yes: a bolt-in fuse can replace the strap and makes U a protected section of the + bus. The best fit is the Bussmann AMG (MEGA-type) fuse: M8 studs on 2.00 in (50.8 mm) centres, 100–300 A, 32 VDC, 1,000 A interrupt rating. B rev 3's link studs are set to 50.8 mm, so the strap or the fuse fits the same studs.
  • Size compared with the strap. Strap: 70.8 × 20 × 6 mm aluminium. AMG: 68.4 mm long, copper terminals 15.4 wide × 1.52 thick with ø8.6 holes, and a 29.2 mm-long, 9 mm-tall plastic body in the middle. So the footprint is nearly the same, but the body hangs below the terminals. That is why B rev 3 has deeper notches and a relief in the U bar.
  • Other flat fuses don't drop in. ANL fuses use about 2.43 in (~62 mm) stud centres (distributor listings, no maker drawing found), so they would need a different stud spacing and more room. MIDI/AMI (30–150 A) uses smaller ø5.5 mm holes, and I couldn't confirm its hole spacing from the datasheet, so it isn't designed in. A Toyota-style fusible link is a plug-in cartridge in its own holder (or a length of fusible wire), not a bolt-down part, so it doesn't fit here.
  • How to use it:
    • Fuse only the U→+ position. The ground (U→−) side stays a plain strap.
    • Rate the fuse to protect the thinnest wire on U. AMG starts at 100 A, which only suits heavy wire. With 8 AWG (60 A per the harness gauge rule) on a U stud, that circuit still needs its own downstream fuse.
    • Check the 1,000 A interrupt rating against the battery's short-circuit current; the trunk MEGA 300 A upstream is the main protection.
  • Sources: Bussmann AMG catalogue pages (bolt-in fuse protection p.35, AMG series p.20); ANL stud centres from a distributor listing; Bussmann AMI datasheet (chipdip copy).

Electrical isolation from the car body (all versions)

  • Every conductor (bars, stud heads, set screws, the link strap) sits on a solid printed floor at least 4.0 mm thick, with no holes through it under any conductor.
  • Bars are held down from the top into blind brass heat-set inserts that end inside plastic. The M6 mounting screws pass only through the plastic end flanges and never touch a conductor.
  • Measured in Fusion for each version: conductor → mounting face 4.0 mm solid ASA; conductor → M6 screw/washer 8.0 mm (straight line, cover off, wall in between).
  • Creepage ≥ 15 mm to the mounting face and ≥ 13 mm to the screw washer. IEC 60664-1 asks for about 1.9 mm at ≤50 V, pollution degree 3.

Engineering notes (all versions)

  • Lugs (Klauke R-series, tin-plated Cu): 1/0 → 6R10 (M10, b 20, l 39); 4 AWG → 4R8 (M8, b 16, l 32); 8 AWG → 2R8 (M8, b 15, l 25). Lugs are at least 4 mm apart, with no stacking.
  • Pole barrier: a 4 mm printed wall up to the cover, with a 24–32 mm metal gap. That is a big margin for a dropped spanner or a loose lug, not just to meet the standard.
  • Current: 6061-T6 at 250 A runs 0.3–0.7 A/mm², a few kelvin rise inside the cover. Bolted joints dominate, so check under 5 mV drop per joint at 250 A. 6101-T6 cuts the losses by about 25%. The B rev 2 link strap is 120 mm².
  • Plastic: ASA, stiff to about 95 °C and UV-stable. No PA-CF, because carbon fibre is partly conductive.
  • Aluminium to copper: tin-plated lugs and ferrules; bare (not anodized), scuffed faces with anti-oxidant paste; stainless conical washers to hold clamp load.

Check before cutting metal

  • Glove-box space (with flanges): A rev 3 274 × 96, B rev 3 345 × 120 mm (older versions: A rev 2 262, B rev 1 261, B rev 2 325 mm long), plus about 45 mm wire room where wires exit.
  • Test-crimp a 6R10 on the real 1/0 cable (bore 10.0 mm), and caliper a 6R10 / 4R8 / 2R8 tongue against the 3 mm pocket depth.
  • Pocket corners: pick an end mill (6 mm or smaller) and the corner radii get added to the model.
  • Check the wire-exit openings (W×H, etched on each cover) against your cable insulation OD.

Sources: Klauke "Tubular cable lugs, Cu, standard type" (R series); Weidmüller H50,0/25 datasheet 1988780000; ISO 4017 / 4032 / 7089 / 7380, DIN 6796; IEC 60664-1; st185-link-ecu-config ENGINE-ROOM-POWER-REDISTRIBUTION.md §5.1/§8.1 and the harness files.
